sections.body: Ansor automatically generates high-performance tensor programs for DNN subgraphs from high-level computation definitions, but its automation is bounded by static known shapes, dense operators, and backend-supported instruction optimization.
sections.heading: Automation and limits in Ansor

sections.body: The same automation theme appears in other domains: distributed quantum compilers map quantum algorithms to networked processors under communication constraints, WCC integrates static timing analysis into C compilation, and the Seesaw Compiler translates digital logic into DNA strand displacement circuits with simulation code and DNA sequences.
sections.heading: Automation in other domains

sections.body: A synthesis page could compare where automation ends in each system: tensor-shape and backend limits for Ansor, Bell-state and topology limits for quantum compilation, timing-analysis contracts for WCC, and impurity or calibration limits for DNA circuit construction.
sections.heading: Boundary comparison
